findings.evidence: False positive for this data type. DrawerFragment.kt:181 calls packageManager.getPackageInfo(requireContext().packageName, 0).versionName, which reads only the app's own version and passes it to the DrawerMenu composable as the label "v$version" (line 190). It does not enumerate installed apps: no getInstalledPackages/getInstalledApplications at this site, and no QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES permission or <queries> element in any app manifest (the only <queries> is in macro-benchmark). The nearby DrawerFragment.kt:117 getLaunchIntentForPackage("by.mev") checks one hardcoded package on a user tap on the settings icon and only starts that activity; the result is not stored or sent. No off-device sink was found.
findings.recommendation: No Data Safety declaration is needed for Apps on device. DrawerFragment.kt:117 is a leftover hardcoded launch of by.mev: without a <queries> entry it resolves to null on Android 11+, so consider removing it as dead behavior.

findings.evidence: The permission is requested but no location is ever read. GamesFragment.kt:50 selects NEARBY_WIFI_DEVICES on Android 13+ and ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION only below it, because the platform requires that permission for Wi-Fi Direct peer discovery; the code comment on line 49 says so. The grant result goes only to viewModel.onWifiDirectPermission(granted) (lines 51, 65), a boolean forwarded to party.onWifiDirectPermission (GamesViewModel.kt:118). A search of main sources for LocationManager, FusedLocation, getLastKnownLocation, requestLocationUpdates and android.location returned no matches, and WifiDirectImpl.kt has no location access, so no coordinates exist to be sent. AppPermission.kt:11 belongs to the standalone demo app in feature/games/xo/demo, which app/build.gradle.kts does not depend on, so it does not ship in the release. It only checks and requests the permissions, then calls onPermissionGranted().
findings.recommendation: No Data Safety declaration is needed for Precise location. Add android:maxSdkVersion="32" to ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION and ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION in feature/games/xo/domain/impl/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml (lines 11-16): the code requests location only below Android 13, and NEARBY_WIFI_DEVICES already has neverForLocation. This keeps the location permission off newer devices and shrinks the permission surface. The request also fires in GamesFragment.onViewCreated (line 67) as soon as the screen opens, so consider explaining the Wi-Fi Direct reason first on Android 12 and lower, where users see a location prompt.

findings.evidence: These click handlers are navigation, not interaction tracking. ItemPageScreen.kt (lines 99, 352, 379) only passes the item key to the onItemClicked callback, and ItemInfoFragment.kt:57 routes it to openItem, which pushes a fragment. ItemsFragment.kt:46-51 opens the item page and sets a viewed flag through updateViewedByUserFieldForItem, which ends in a local Room update: ItemsDao.kt:29 "UPDATE ItemsTable SET viewedByUser = 1 WHERE name =:name". The item page itself loads from bundled assets (GetItemInfoUseCase.kt:107 readText via res.getAssets, line 111 file:///android_asset image), so opening an item makes no network request. No analytics or crash SDK is present: build files and libs.versions.toml have no Firebase, Crashlytics, AppMetrica, Sentry, Amplitude or ad SDK (the only Google Play services entry is play-services-instantapps), and no logEvent/trackEvent call exists. The custom Logger keeps entries in an in-memory SharedFlow (LoggerImpl.kt:14-23), and its main-source consumers are on-screen log views, with no upload path seen in LoggerImpl. Tapping play on an ability sound (ItemInfoFragment.onPlayClicked) streams a static audioUrl, which is a content fetch and carries no interaction payload.
findings.recommendation: No Data Safety declaration is needed for App interactions. Keep the viewed flag local. If an analytics or crash SDK is added later, update the Play Data safety form first, because the current form declares no data collected.
